mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility (rising from -45.1% to -36.1% over four weeks) signals resumption of commuting patterns that generate incidental retail visits during work-week transit, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 9 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 18.6% to 13.7%) indicates people are spending less time at home, implying increased out-of-home activity. This behavioral shift directly increases RETAIL_REC visits over the next two weeks as people resume discretionary shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 4.9 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility stabilizes or rises in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week in at least 2 of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility recovery (from -58.7% to -48.4%) combined with WORKPLACES recovery creates a multiplier effect: commuters using transit generate retail footfall both at transit hubs and destination neighborhoods, amplifying RETAIL_REC gains over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved over the observation window
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES reverses by >8 percentage points in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean over t+1 to t+4 is not higher than t-3 to t-0 mean.

mechanism_narrative: December holiday shopping behavior (decision point is 2020-12-15) drives RETAIL_REC upward independent of other mobility signals. The seasonal effect overrides current suppression levels, producing positive direction over the next four weeks despite ongoing restrictions.
evidence_refs: fact:decision time point is 2020-12-15, peak holiday shopping season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over t+1 to t+4 does not exceed RETAIL_REC over t-3 to t-0, or RETAIL_REC falls below -35% in any single week of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls below -50% in week t+1 (indicating tightened restrictions), retail closures or capacity limits will suppress RETAIL_REC below current levels. The mechanism is triggered by policy-driven transit suppression and produces negative direction.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -50.0 percent in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is currently at -48.4%, near the -50% threshold
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains above -50% for all four weeks ahead, or RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT falling below -50%.

mechanism_narrative: Divergence between GROCERY_PHARM stability (declining only -11.4%) and RETAIL_REC suppression (-39.9%) indicates consumers are prioritizing essential shopping over discretionary retail. If this divergence persists, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as essential-only behavior locks in over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC exceeds 25 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:gap between GROCERY_PHARM (-11.4%) and RETAIL_REC (-39.9%) is 28.5 percentage points
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows to below 20 percentage points, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility decline (from -4.9% to -14.3%) signals reduced outdoor leisure activity, suggesting weather deterioration or behavioral shift away from outdoor spaces. This outdoor suppression redirects discretionary activity indoors to retail venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 9.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -10% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week in at least one of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent recovery across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and declining RESIDENTIAL (indicating less home-bound behavior) creates a three-way reinforcement loop: commuting resumes, transit use rises, and people spend less time at home, collectively driving RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks. Mechanism fails if any single component reverses.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series show directional improvement or decline consistent with reopening
failure_condition: Any of WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, or RESIDENTIAL reverses by >5 percentage points in weeks t+1 or t+2, or RETAIL_REC mean over t+1 to t+4 does not exceed mean over t-3 to t-0.
